title: Fifteenth Amendment ratified
mechanism: Barred race as a voting qualification and left enforcement to Congress and the courts.
loop: Loop R4b: Voting rules shape who can hold rule-makers accountable

title: Mississippi adopts its 1890 constitution
mechanism: Literacy tests, poll taxes and understanding clauses (which let registrars judge whether an applicant could explain the constitution) spread across the South, and Black registration collapsed within a decade.
loop: Loop R4b: Voting rules shape who can hold rule-makers accountable
source_text: Mississippi Constitution of 1890, art. 12; Kousser, The Shaping of Southern Politics (1974)

title: Seventeenth Amendment ratified
mechanism: Senators became directly elected; each state kept two senators regardless of population.
loop: Loop R12: Entrenched majorities shape courts that rule on election rules

title: Nineteenth Amendment ratified
mechanism: Barred sex as a voting qualification; the eligible electorate roughly doubled on paper.
loop: Loop B4: Electoral consequences can improve public performance

title: Reapportionment Act of 1929 fixes the House at 435
mechanism: Average district size grew from about 210,000 to about 760,000 people, which reduced constituents' access to their member and how closely seats track population.
loop: Outside driver X2: Population patterns and residential sorting (no named loop); related reform R-46: Expand the House of Representatives

title: Wagner Act (and the Social Security Act, August 14, 1935)
mechanism: Created collective bargaining rights and social insurance, with agricultural and domestic workers excluded.
loop: Loop R6: Weak bargaining power and concentrated wealth reinforce each other

title: Taft-Hartley Act passed over a veto
mechanism: Allowed state right-to-work laws and barred secondary boycotts; union growth stopped in the South.
loop: Loop R6: Weak bargaining power and concentrated wealth reinforce each other

title: Reynolds v. Sims (with Baker v. Carr, 1962, and Wesberry v. Sanders, 1964)
mechanism: Established one person, one vote for state legislatures and House districts, ending the overrepresentation of rural areas.
loop: Loop B4: Electoral consequences can improve public performance

title: Voting Rights Act signed
mechanism: Required federal approval (preclearance) of voting changes in covered places and sent federal examiners; Black registration in the South rose from about 30% to over 60% by 1970.
loop: Loop R4b: Voting rules shape who can hold rule-makers accountable

title: McGovern-Fraser rules take effect
mechanism: Binding primaries and caucuses replaced bargaining at party conventions, so primary voters became the people who choose nominees.
loop: Loop R10: Safe seats shift accountability to small primary electorates
source_text: Commission on Party Structure and Delegate Selection, Mandate for Reform (1970); Shafer, Quiet Revolution (1983)

title: Congressional Budget and Impoundment Control Act (Federal Election Campaign Act amendments, October 15, 1974)
mechanism: Made it unlawful for the President to withhold appropriated money without a rescission approved by Congress; the campaign-finance amendments set contribution limits and created the Federal Election Commission.
loop: Loop R18: Weakening watchdogs lowers the cost of further unilateral action

title: Buckley v. Valeo
mechanism: Struck down spending limits and kept contribution limits; treating campaign money as speech has framed the law for fifty years.
loop: Loop R1b: Political spending and court rulings reinforce each other

title: Proposition 13 (labor-law reform filibustered June 22, 1978; First National Bank of Boston v. Bellotti, April 26, 1978)
mechanism: The California tax revolt, the defeat of labor-law reform in the Senate and new corporate speech rights arrived in one season.
loop: Loop R1: Wealth and political influence reinforce each other
source_text: Cal. Const. art. XIII A; 124 Cong. Rec. 18,398 (1978); 435 U.S. 765

title: Inspector General Act (Ethics in Government Act, October 26, 1978)
mechanism: Created statutory watchdogs inside agencies and required financial disclosure by officials.
loop: Loop B1a: Independent oversight can limit policy favoritism

title: The 104th Congress opens
mechanism: The House cut committee staff by about 41% (2,147 in 1993 to 1,266 in 1995), Congress closed the Office of Technology Assessment and party leaders took more control; expectations that committee members raise money followed.
loop: Loop R2: Congress becomes dependent on outside expertise
source_text: H.Res. 6 (104th); Brookings Vital Statistics on Congress, ch. 5

title: Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (Commodity Futures Modernization Act, December 21, 2000)
mechanism: Allowed banks, securities firms and insurers to combine, and the 2000 law left most derivatives unregulated; the 2008 crisis and the TARP bank rescue followed.
loop: Loop R1: Wealth and political influence reinforce each other

title: Citizens United v. FEC (SpeechNow.org v. FEC, March 26, 2010)
mechanism: Independent spending by corporations and unions became unlimited; super PACs followed within two months.
loop: Loop R1b: Political spending and court rulings reinforce each other

title: Shelby County v. Holder
mechanism: Struck down the formula that decided which places needed preclearance, which ended preclearance in practice; Texas moved to enforce its voter-ID law the same day.
loop: Loop R4b: Voting rules shape who can hold rule-makers accountable

title: Nuclear option for lower-court and executive nominations (extended to the Supreme Court on April 6, 2017)
mechanism: A rules change by simple majority ended the 60-vote threshold for these confirmations, so appointments track which party controls the Senate.
loop: Loop R12: Entrenched majorities shape courts that rule on election rules
source_text: Congressional Record, Nov. 21, 2013, S8417; Apr. 6, 2017, S2390

title: Tax Cuts and Jobs Act
mechanism: Cut the corporate rate to 21% and made the individual cuts temporary; the resulting deficits fed later arguments for spending cuts.
loop: Loop R1: Wealth and political influence reinforce each other

title: Electoral Count Reform Act
mechanism: Made the Vice President's role in the count ministerial, required one-fifth of each chamber to raise an objection, made governors' certificates conclusive and sped up court review.
loop: Loop B4: Electoral consequences can improve public performance

title: 2025 budget reconciliation law, P.L. 119-21 (counter-event: the American Rescue Plan, March 11, 2021)
mechanism: The 2025 law extends the 2017 tax cuts and, by Congressional Budget Office estimates tallied by KFF, cuts federal Medicaid spending by about $1 trillion over 2025 to 2034, with further cuts to SNAP food aid. The 2021 law expanded the child tax credit for one year, when child poverty under the Supplemental Poverty Measure fell to 5.2%; the expansion then expired.
loop: Loop R5: Financial strain narrows who takes part in policy decisions

title: Louisiana v. Callais
mechanism: The Supreme Court (6 to 3) held that Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act is violated only when the evidence supports a strong inference of intentional discrimination. Within five weeks Florida, Tennessee and Louisiana enacted new congressional maps and the Court let Alabama return to its 2023 plan; each change removed a majority-Black or Black-opportunity district.
loop: Loop R4b: Voting rules shape who can hold rule-makers accountable

mechanism: Trump v. Slaughter overruled Humphrey's Executor and lets the President remove Federal Trade Commission members at will (6 to 3). The same day, in Trump v. FEC struck down limits on party committees' coordinated spending.
